episodes.178920: Several consecutive days of significant severe weather impacted eastern New Mexico from May 24-26, 2023. Showers and thunderstorms developed along the dryline and east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains on May 23rd. Storms tracked east and southeast across the eastern plains of New Mexico. Extensive severe weather was reported when these storms encountered greater moisture and lift closer to the Texas border. Hail up to 3.5 inches in diameter, thunderstorm wind gusts of 80 to 90 mph, and three tornados were reported in an area stretching from Union County to Roosevelt County. The largest hail stones and strongest wind gusts focused throughout Curry County during the evening hours. Hail and wind damage was reported in Tucumcari, Grady, and Clovis. Three separate tornadoes were reported in northern Curry County. Thunderstorms also dropped very heavy rainfall of 2 to 4 inches of rain across portions of Quay, De Baca, Curry, and Roosevelt Counties. Urban flooding occurred in Clovis, NM, causing some roads to be closed, and some cars to be stranded. Severe weather continued through the night and into May 25th with numerous reports of large hail, strong winds, and flash flooding. Quay County was particularly hard hit with baseball size hail and torrential rainfall amounts in excess of 5 inches. Significant hail damage was reported across Tucumcari with widespread flooding across the county. Severe wind gusts of 70 to 80 mph were common with these storms with damage reported. Strong to severe storms continued well into the night once again on the 25th with more heavy rainfall around the Caprock. The focus for severe weather shifted farther west on May 26th with large hail and heavy rainfall reported around Torrance County. A tornado and baseball size hail was also reported with a supercell near Encino. This activity spread eastward through the day with large hail, damaging wind gusts, and more torrential rainfall around the Caprock well into the night of May 26th. Three-day rainfall amounts exceeded 6 inches in many parts of Curry and Quay counties.
episodes.179011: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.179108: A strong trough produced heavy rainfall occurred over Tutuila on May 26th between 300 and 700SST to cause widespread flooding over the island. The rainfall produced numerous landslides across the island.
episodes.179233: A tight pressure gradient between a strong trough and a ridge produced high sustained winds and wind gusts between 330 and 650SST on May 26th. WSO Pago Pago recorded sustained winds of 30 MPH or more and gusts of 35 MPH or more during that time. Maximum recorded winds at WSO Pago Pago reached 36 MPH with gusts reaching 45 MPH at 350SST. Higher gusts of 60 MPH or more are estimated in areas of funneling winds across Tutuila.
episodes.179321: Line of thunderstorms developed in northern Colorado just east of Interstate 25 moving northeast into central Laramie County where quarter size hail was reported on the east side of Cheyenne. Wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph were reported with this line of storms farther north and east. Additional storms developed along the North Laramie Range with sub-severe hail near Douglas.
episodes.179331: Broad quasi-stationary upper-level trough situated over western  CONUS lingered for several days and led to persistent southwesterly flow aloft and daily showers and thunderstorms across portions of Southwest, Central, and North-central Montana, some of which were severe, producing strong gusty winds and significant hail.
episodes.179354: A strong thunderstorm produced hail to penny size in far northeastern Campbell County.
episodes.179355: A strong thunderstorm developed over northern Lawrence County, producing hail to penny size south of Spearfish.
episodes.179409: Afternoon and evening sea breeze thunderstorms produced waterspouts in waters offshore St. Petersburg in West Central Florida and Boca Grande in Southwest Florida.
episodes.179421: A pacific disturbance would end up setting off another round of thunderstorms, with some reaching severe levels.
episodes.179489: Thunderstorms early in the morning on the 25th kept conditions relatively stable on the afternoon of the 25th which prevented thunderstorms from developing over the region. However, another round of thunderstorms did develop across the higher terrain of northeast New Mexico and moved to the southeast across the South Plains early in the morning on the 26th. The activity eventually accelerated southeastward, sweeping across much of the central and southern South Plains and Rolling Plains through the rest of the morning. A few severe wind gusts were reported in Lubbock County as well as extensive street flooding.
episodes.179574: Thunderstorms developed along a surface trough over western North Dakota, with some of the storms becoming severe. One note of interest with these storms was that the strongest ones exhibited anticyclonic rotation, with multiple splitting storms. The largest hail reported was ping-pong ball size, which fell in far northern McKenzie County, just south of Lake Sakakawea. NWS received no reports of damage from the hail.
episodes.180032: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced some large hail near Sheridan.
episodes.180038: An isolated thunderstorm produced some quarter size hail.
episodes.180237: In the afternoon of the 25th, slow moving, high precipitation thunderstorms formed in eastern Colorado and moved northeast. In the evening, severe hail was reported along with heavy rain. Overnight on the 25th, the storms slowed, began to back-build, and cause flooding in southwest Nebraska. Flooding continued until the 28th but the damage it caused took even longer to repair. 6.5 to 9.5 inches of rain was reported across Dundy, Hitchcock and Red Willow counties.
episodes.180345: Weak upper-level disturbances migrated across South Florida, which including daytime heating, brought strong thunderstorms to the interior and Lake Okeechobee areas on May 26th.
episodes.180346: As a mid-level trough persisted over the Florida Panhandle, abundant low-level moisture and diurnal heating led to plenty of instability in the atmosphere on May 26th. Numerous slow-moving showers and thunderstorms formed in the afternoon across the Miami metro.
episodes.180429: In the late morning of the 25th, a line of storms from eastern Kansas restrengthened as they slowly moved northwest. These storms dumped upwards of 6 inches of rain near Hoxie and caused flooding in various locations in northwest Kansas. As the day progressed, more storms began firing to the west from the outflow of this initial system. In the afternoon of the 25th, these new slow moving, high precipitation thunderstorms forming across eastern Colorado and northwest Kansas moved northeast. Overnight on the 25th, the storms began to back-build, and cause flooding in extreme northwest Kansas. Flooding continued until at least the 28th but the damage it caused took even longer to repair.
episodes.180502: Isolated but strong thunderstorms developed near Long Key, producing a waterspout and storm-force wind gusts.  A negatively-tilted upper trough was positioned over the southeastern United States with a surface low moving northeast in the Atlantic.
episodes.180516: Several reports of land spouts and funnel clouds occurred on May 26th, May 27th, and May 31st, 2023 near Star, ID and Twin Falls, ID. The radar signatures for both events were unremarkable, leading to the conclusion that these vortices were likely originating from low level and surface directional wind shear and cumulus congestus clouds on the fringes of larger thunderstorms.
episodes.180570: During the early morning hours of May 26th, very heavy rain fell across southern portions of Chase and Hayes counties in southwestern Nebraska. The heavy rainfall led to flash flooding over southern Chase and southern Hayes counties in Nebraska. Highway 6 and highway 61 were closed in southeastern Chase County due to water covering the roadway. Highway 25 and highway 6 was also closed in southern Hayes County due to flooding.
episodes.180632: A lot of strong storms came through the area.
episodes.180679: A pattern developed by late May with sufficient moisture and forcing to yield scattered showers and thunderstorms almost every day, generally from the afternoon on into the early evening hours. Some of these storms were strong, yielding damaging wind gusts and hail. Additionally, a road washout was reported as a result of continued spring runoff from the prior winter's record snowfall.
episodes.180734: A shortwave trough moved across Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms to many locations across western and central Wyoming. The most notable storm occurred in northern Fremont County where a very strong thunderstorm gust front caused damage at a campground on the northeastern shore of Boysen Reservoir. Hail of quarter to half dollar size was reported in Big Horn, Fremont, Park and Sweetwater Counties.
episodes.180795: During the late evening of May 25th a line of thunderstorms moved into the northwest combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles moving south to southeast into much of the western combined Panhandles. One of the storms became severe producing hail upwards of 1.5 in diameter near Texline, Texas. As this line of storms continued southward, discrete supercell storms developed in eastern New Mexico around the I-40 corridor. As the line of storms from the north moved south of I-40 west of Amarillo and met up with the storms in New Mexico the system slowed down a little and produced some heavy rainfall causing some flooding problems in Deaf Smith and Randall Counties.
episodes.180857: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and strong winds as they moved across northern part of the Denver metro area.  The hail ranged from nickel to ping pong ball size.  A brief wind gust to 60 mph was observed in Morgan County.  In addition, two weak tornadoes touched down in Morgan and Washington counties.  No damage was observed.
episodes.180884: A long-track complex of thunderstorms developed off of the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico and moved southeast. This complex produced severe wind gusts across the northern Permian Basin early that morning. Additional thunderstorms developed across portions of the higher elevations of the Davis Mountains later that afternoon. Severe winds and flash flooding were observed with these thunderstorms.
episodes.180886: A shortwave trough over the Central Rocky Mountains and an active sub-tropical jet stream aided in the development of numerous supercells over the higher elevations of the Davis Mountains, Glass Mountains, and Big Bend region.  A couple of additional thunderstorms develop across portions of the Permian Basin. Several reports of large hail, damaging winds, and a landspout tornado were received.
episodes.181342: Ample low level moisture aided in creating an incredibly unstable environment with enough wind shear to create severe thunderstorms and some landspout tornadoes.
episodes.181368: Storms produced a weak tornado and large hail in Cassia County.
episodes.181398: Another Low brought thunderstorms to the region bringing heavy rains and lightning for May 27, 2023.

events.county: Coastal Waters From Bonita Beach To Englewood Fl Out 20 Nm
events.narrative: Broadcast media relayed picture of waterspout approximately 15 miles offshore west of Cayo Costa.
Emergency manager reported that county road 11 is covered 50 yards wide with near 6 inches of water.
Reported from the Broadcast Media.
TxDot El Paso reported flooding of Comanche Creek and Ranch Road 170.
The Gunnison Island mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 60 mph as a result of outflow winds associated with a nearby cluster of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area.

There were multiple reports from storm chasers of large hail ranging in size from 2 to 3.5 inches just east-northeast of Tucumcari along U.S. Highway 54. Thankfully there were no reports of damage directly related to the hail.
A trained spotter reported hail up to the size of quarters.
Caller estimated hail mainly from pea to penny in size. They said that there were a few larger stones around a quarter in size.
The Tucumcari Airport measured a thunderstorm wind gusts of 61 to 75 mph during this timeframe.
Thunderstorm wind gust to 82 mph measured via anemometer on car roof by a storm chaser along U.S. Highway 278 southeast of Tucumcari.
Public report of thunderstorm wind damage equivalent to downed tree limbs and blown shingles off. No actual reports of damage to estimate from.

Multiple reports of flash flooding were received via social media during the evening of May 25, 2023. Streets throughout town were flooded, closed, or impassable with vehicles being stranded in some spots. Water was also reported to have reached up to business entrances.
Law enforcement reported flooding under the 6th St. underpass with a vehicle stuck in the flood waters.

Emergency manager reported Highway 34 and 61 were both closed due to flash flooding. Highway 34 was closed from Benkelman to Trenton while highway 61 was closed from Benkelman to Enders. Up to 8 feet of water over the road was reported by Fire and Rescue. At least one car and driver were stranded in the water and a secondary road was completely washed out. The eastern portion of Dundy county remained largely under water for the following days.
An off-duty NWS meteorologist storm chasing measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 59 mph.
The NMDOT reported State Highway 93 being closed due to standing water over the roadway south of I-40 to Endee. There were no reports of any damage.

In around around Stratton, at least one home and multiple cars were being swept away from flash flooding. Water rescues were required to save at least 4 citizens inside their homes. The town of Palisade also had extensive flooding but to less of an extent than Stratton. Highway 34 from Benkelman to Trenton was closed due to flooding. Highway 25 from Trenton to highway 6 was also closed.  The first report of flash flooding was when a driver became stranded near Palisade and needed rescue.
A mesonet station in Clovis measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 64 mph.

events.county: Bayside And Gulfside From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge
events.narrative: A wind gust of 57 knots was measured at Long Key Light.
Highway 6 southeast of Imperial is closed with water over the roadway.
The parking lot of Dameron Park was flooded.  Around  2 inches of rain was measured in 30 minutes by local ground observation stations.
Roadways are impassable due to flood waters along County Road L in Clovis.
Highway 6 near Hamlet is closed due to water over the roadway.

A swath of severe thunderstorm winds were observed from just north of Shallowater to Lubbock International Airport. A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Shallowater measured severe wind gusts to 59 mph from 0710 CST through 0711 CST. The Automated Surface Observing System at Lubbock International Airport measured a severe wind gust to 62 mph.
Gordon Cummings Road was flooded due to  heavy rainfall and the overflowing of local creeks.  A water rescue did occur along this road.
Motorist stranded on Highway 6 due to high water over the roadway.

A severe thunderstorm which brought severe winds to Lubbock County also caused flash flooding around the city of Lubbock. Numerous roads in Lubbock became flooded from heavy rainfall in a short amount of time.
Several campers reported stranded due to high water from flash flooding.

At 8:35, dispatch reported multiple roads under water in Herndon. Over the following hours, conditions worsened dramatically. The town of Herndon became completely cutoff and surrounded by flood waters. These flash flood waters also put a levee upstream of the town to become at risk of failing, which would have flooded the town. Thankfully, the levee held and was able to be reinforced in the afternoon hours. North of Ludell, at least one country road culvert was completely washed out, making the road impassable.
Highway 61 south of US Highway 6 is closed due to flash flooding.
Highway 25A between Palisade and Highway 25 is closed due to flooding.
The city park and pool is flooded on the north side of Palisade.

Highway 61 remained closed until at least the evening of the 28th when water was still 3 or more feet deep over the road between Benkelman and Enders. Highway 34 between Benkelman and Trenton also remained closed due to flood waters of an unknown depth. Of the parts of the highways and other county road that were starting to be above water on the 28th, washouts and other damage were reported.

Due to high gusts from thunderstorm winds, a power outage occurred for most locations on the east side of Tutuila. The estimated time of the outage was around 430 SST. Power was restored around 900 SST. Estimated wind speeds reached up to 60 knots along some areas of the eastern side of Tutuila.

A powerful thunderstorm wind gust caused a downed tree in the village of Auto during the early morning hours on May 26th. The tree blocked the westbound lane of the main road. Estimated wind gusts reached up to 50 knots.
A powerful thunderstorm wind gust caused a downed tree in the village of Amaua during the early morning hours of May 26th. Estimated wind gusts reached up to 50 knots.

Emergency management reported a landslide during the early morning hours on May 26th in the village of Amouli due to heavy rainfall. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

Emergency management reported a landslide during the early morning hours on May 26th in the village of Masausi due to heavy rainfall. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

Emergency management reported a landslide during the early morning hours on May 26th in the village of Afao due to heavy rainfall. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

Emergency management reported a landslide during the early morning hours on May 26th between the villages of Fagamutu and Atauloma due to heavy rainfall. Large rocks and dirt covered both the eastbound and westbound lanes. Due to no radar coverage and no rain gage data in the area, no accurate rainfall depth or intensity is available.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A waterspout was observed approximately 5 miles to the south of Long Key.

Barnett Park in McCook flooded due to the Republican River rising out of its banks. It remained flooded until the afternoon of the 28th. Highway 34 and 83 both had to be closed due to the river flooding over them.

Highway 34 from Benkelman to Trenton was closed due to flooding. Highway 25 from Trenton to highway 6 was also closed. The train bridge west of Stratton was washed out due to the flooding. A road grader was also found to be almost fully submerged.
The Frenchman creek was reported to be out of its bank and flooding county multiple roads, although it seemingly never flooded over highway 6.

A broadcast media member reported flooding across a few roadways and parking lots in South Miami Heights due to heavy rainfall in the area. Rainfall amounts were in the 2 to 4 inch range, most of it falling in 2 hours or less.

events.county: Volusia-Brevard County Line To Sebastian Inlet 0-20Nm
events.narrative: Weatherflow station at Melbourne Beach Barrier Island Sanctuary (XMBI) measured a 34 knot wind gust from the north-northwest.
The Florida Institute of Technology weather station at Sebastian Inlet measured a 35 knot wind gust from the northwest.
A trained spotter reported one inch hail near Amsterdam, ID.
Public photos indicated approximately nickel-sized hail near Tabiona.
A photo submitted on social media from a trained spotter showed a funnel cloud just northeast of his location.
The public reported quarter size hail to the northwest of Rock Springs.
There was a CoCoRaHS report of 1.5 inch hail that caused unknown minor damage.
SFWMD mesonet station LZ40 reported a peak wind gust of 41 knots / 47 mph as a thunderstorm moved over Lake Okeechobee.
Tornado photographed east of Almo.   No damage occurred as it was in open fields.
A trained spotter reported 1 inch hail along Highway 14 to the east of Cody.

Lanspout: A landspout tornado developed around 408 PM CDT about 20 miles northwest of Marfa, TX, and was on the ground for approximately one minute. A second developed shortly after the first, dissipating within 10 to 15 seconds. No damage was reported. Path details are estimates.
The WeatherStem station at the House of Refuge measured a 35 knot wind gust from the west-northwest.
A 59 mph wind gust was reported at the ASOS at the Fremont County airport near Riverton.
Land spout tornado reported by public. No damage or injuries reported.
A trained spotter reported hail that was measured at 1.25 inches.
The WeatherStem station at the House of Refuge measured a 36 knot wind gust from the northeast.
Funnel cloud photograph received west of American Falls.
Received report from mPING.
The Weatherflow site at Jungle Trail measured a 37 knot wind gust from the northeast.
Received report from mPING.
Funnel cloud photographed west of American Falls.
A trained spotter reported 1 inch hail along Gas Hills Road to the east of Riverton.

Very strong winds occurred with a thunderstorm outflow gust front on Boysen Reservoir As the gust front hit the northeastern shore near the marina, the winds tipped several campers setup at a campground, at least two of which were severely damaged. The winds also blew a carport over 100 yards. A NWS storm survey determined that straight line wind speeds of 70 to 80 mph likely caused the damage. No injuries were reported with this event.
Reported from broadcast media.
Reported from broadcast media.
A trained spotter reported half dollar size hail the southwest of Byron, WY.
Photograph of funnel cloud.
Received report via Facebook that occurred at Interstate 80 mile marker 372 at the Port of Entry.

In the afternoon of the 26th, the waters had stopped rising, but the town of Herndon was cutoff by all land routes until the late morning of the 27th, when all but one road became traversable. Multiple county roads were also submerged for days later, however on the 30th, flooding conditions subsided and no more roads were reported underwater, although there were many that had been washed out and destoryed.
Reported from the public.
Half-dollar-size hail was reported near Fort Davis.
A roof was partially blown off of a shed with minor tree damage in the area. Wind speeds are estimated to have been around 70 mph. Property damage is an estimate.
There was a brief 15 to 20 second spin up along a converging outflow boundaries.
Reported from a trained spotter.
Reported by a storm chaser.
A tornado touched down in an open field.  No damage was observed.
Received report of dime to penny size hail.
Funnel cloud witnessed by NWS personnel and noted in a pilot report during a climb out of nearby Great Falls International Airport. Location estimated.
One inch diameter hail was observed at McDonald Observatory.
A trained spotter reported a rope tornado just south of their location in Encino, NM. No damage was reported.
Relayed report by broadcast media. Time estimated from radar.
Dime to golf ball size hail was reported near Pleasant Hill, NM.
